identity.title: Foundation Model Insights and a Multi-Model Approach for Superior Fine-Grained One-shot Subset Selection

problem.claim: The work studies how to select informative one-shot training subsets using foundation-model-based information extractors across datasets of differing granularity.

gap.claim: Traditional information extractors are dataset-dependent, and it is unclear whether foundation models outperform them broadly or whether all foundation models are equally suitable for subset selection.

contributions.claim: Reports that foundation models consistently outperform traditional information extractors on fine-grained datasets, but their advantage diminishes on coarse-grained datasets with noisy labels.
Proposes RAM-APL, which uses multiple foundation models and their complementary strengths for subset selection on fine-grained image datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present RAM-APL as a foundation-model-based, multi-model approach tailored to fine-grained image subset selection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent foundation-model gains over traditional information extractors on fine-grained datasets, with reduced gains on coarse-grained datasets with noisy labels.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance for RAM-APL on Oxford-IIIT Pet, Food-101, and Caltech-UCSD Birds-200-2011.

narrative_sequence.summary: One-shot subset selection is framed as a way to reduce training costs by identifying informative data through an information extractor.
Traditional extractors are described as target-dataset-dependent, motivating questions about foundation-model superiority and variation across foundation models.
Experiments are reported to show a granularity- and label-noise-dependent pattern: stronger foundation-model advantages on fine-grained data and weaker advantages on coarse-grained noisy-label data.
The paper introduces multi-foundation-model RAM-APL for fine-grained images and reports state-of-the-art results on three named datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the reported advantage of foundation models to dataset granularity and label noise, rather than presenting one uniformly favorable result.

lessons.interpretation: Performance claims can be made more informative by stating the data conditions under which the advantage changes.
lessons.application: When presenting a method comparison, stratify results by salient dataset properties such as granularity and label noise, and state where the advantage weakens.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when those properties are not measured, are not relevant to the task, or the study design cannot support stratified comparisons.

source_observation.claim: RAM-APL is motivated by complementary strengths across multiple foundation models and operationalizes that motivation in a named ranking method.

lessons.interpretation: A multi-model proposal is easier to understand when its design is explicitly tied to an observed limitation or heterogeneity.
lessons.application: For an ensemble or multi-model method, identify the complementary behavior being exploited and connect it directly to the method's aggregation or ranking rule.
lessons.exception: Do not use this pattern when models are redundant or when the abstract provides no evidence or rationale for complementarity.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify subset sizes, datasets and baselines used in the broader experiments, metrics, numerical gains, foundation-model identities, or statistical uncertainty.
The state-of-the-art claim is author-reported; the comparison scope and evaluation conditions are not given.
The abstract does not establish that RAM-APL's reported gains are caused specifically by model complementarity.
